f14_verification.claim_under_test: the cancelled-worker failure mode has no direct regression test
f14_verification.method: restored the pre-d3f5458 dispatch at all five run_worker sites in a throwaway copy of HEAD, leaving today's tests intact, and ran tests/tui
f14_verification.result: 45/45 PASSED with the defect present — the finding is confirmed, and stronger than stated

self_correction.false_claim: d3f5458 and its receipt stated that pyproject's filterwarnings entry made 'coroutine ... was never awaited' a suite failure
self_correction.truth: it does not fire. The un-awaited coroutine is collected by the garbage collector, so the warning arrives through the unraisable hook wrapped as PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning and never passes through that filter.
self_correction.how_found: the F14 experiment above; the guard was written, looked correct, and did nothing
self_correction.replacement: error::pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning, measured FAILING the suite with the pre-fix dispatch restored before being called a guard

new_test_labelled_honestly: tests/tui/test_app.py::test_dispatched_work_actually_runs_and_is_not_silently_dropped drives the selection worker with no refresh_all() to mask it. Its docstring states it is NOT the d3f5458 regression test and gives the measurement: it passes with the pre-fix dispatch too, because a worker that actually starts awaits a bare coroutine fine.
